note: P4140 (Pro 20:17) — bread gained by deceit is sweet, but afterward the mouth is full of gravel.

dims.v: deceit — bread by fraud, sweet then bitter as gravel
the deceit by which bread is gained — sweet at first, but afterward the mouth is full of gravel
the fraud whose sweetness turns to grit

sheqer (falsehood/deceit) — 'bread gained by DECEIT is sweet to a man, but afterward his mouth will be full of gravel'; ill-gotten gain is delicious at first but ends bitter — a mouthful of gravel. The deceptive arc of dishonest gain (cf 9:17). Sweet now, grit later.
